I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match my irrigation capacity, and protect my income. At the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so my job now is to manage it carefully through spring water and fertilizer, control disease and aphids if pressure appears, and push for a stable grain yield rather than gamble on a higher-cost crop. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize immediately to catch heat and rainfall, use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen to support ear formation, and keep the field clean and well-timed on water and pest control. I am educated, so I will manage inputs with discipline: not too little, not excessive, and I will stay with crops and practices that fit my county, my age, and the need for steady output from each mu.
